# SuperBench

> One task, one bench: a bench is one task's git worktree, leased to one holder and checkpointed to the remote between turns. SuperBench v0.0.2, the latest release, is an experimental single-host release for Linux amd64 and trusted repositories.

SuperBench is a command-line tool (`bench`) and a local daemon that create a git worktree for each task, lease it to one holder at a time, checkpoint it and release it. A checkpoint pushes the bench's existing HEAD to its branch without force and confirms the remote has exactly that commit; it never creates a commit, and a dirty or untracked tree is refused. Leases are cooperative: they stop other `bench` acquisitions, not direct edits or other processes running as the same user, and they never expire on their own. On a managed Linux host with a dedicated XFS mount, each bench gets its own byte and inode caps; elsewhere a quota is recorded, not enforced. Benches start from shared git mirrors and shared or checkout-local caches; the shared package store has the same managed-host limits, a failed mirror refresh refuses the lease, and collecting old shared caches is not built yet. A released, clean, remote-confirmed bench can be archived read-only, and deletion waits for a grace period and a person's approval of the exact file list, through local administrative commands; automatic log retention is off until an operator turns it on, and retiring a bench's quota during reap applies only on managed Linux hosts. On Linux, supervised runs are fenced in their own cgroup; that is process-tree fencing, not user or mount isolation, so SuperBench is for trusted repositories only. The CLI and daemon talk over a Unix socket with kernel peer-credential checks, and the source opens no TCP listener (read from the source, not asserted by a test). It depends on no other suite product. SuperBench v0.0.2 (2026-11-23) ships one archive for Linux amd64 holding `bench`, `benchd`, `bench-quota` and `bench-payload`, with SHA256SUMS and a build-provenance attestation, on its GitHub release. It is an experimental single-host release under the MIT licence, not a supported installation: use a disposable or staging host. Over v0.0.1 (2026-11-22), v0.0.2 names up to five of the paths to clean when a checkpoint or release is refused for a dirty tree, and its docs explain workspaces whose repositories a card chooses upstream; the limits are unchanged.

## Not done yet

- Running a task's payload as a separate user (in progress; today there is no user or mount isolation)
- More than one host (moving a bench between hosts is a reviewed administrative step)
- Builds for macOS, arm64 or package managers, a supported installation, and a promise of compatibility between releases
- Automatic lease expiry, remote authentication, a web interface and suite integration
